issues.title: exit gate 0: propose mode proven non-mutating under hostile tools
issues.description:
Phase 0 exit gate. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

One dispatch path is demonstrated AND propose mode is proven non-mutating in an
end-to-end hostile-tool test. If Pi cannot enforce the boundary, mutation stays
disabled pending a sandbox or a safer adapter design.

Required tests (section 5, Phase 0):

- one failure event starts at most one workflow
- a propose-mode event cannot alter project files through native tools, shell
  redirects, subprocesses, or a continuation
- a concurrent user edit is preserved
- process cancellation terminates child work, leaving no orphan

"Hostile" means the test actively tries to escape: shell redirection, a child
tool call, a skill write outside the repo. A test that only checks the happy
path proves nothing here -- br-33co was found by trying to escape on purpose.

This gate cannot pass while br-33co is open.
issues.acceptance_criteria: The hostile-tool suite passes on CI and is not skippable; propose mode alters nothing in the user's tree by any route; cancellation leaves no orphan process.

issues.title: spike: prove what Pi/OMP can actually enforce
issues.description:
Spike 0.2. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Determine whether Pi/OMP can provide per-invocation tool grants and a reliable
approval/cancellation boundary, and whether OS-level isolation or worktree
execution is viable locally. Document residual risks.

Start from the measured answer, not the documented one: `--tools=read,grep,glob`
does NOT restrict tools. A child reported `_read _grep _glob _manage_skill
_learn _write`, and `--no-tools --no-skills` changed nothing. A probe child
created `~/.omp/agent/managed-skills/containment-probe-delete-me/SKILL.md` in
the operator's HOME, which would load in every future session in every repo.
Measured three times; see br-33co.

That makes REQ-SAFE-003 currently unmet and gives the spike a concrete
question: if the grant boundary cannot be enforced at the tool-call layer, what
is the fallback -- OS sandbox, worktree, or keeping mutation disabled?

Section 7: do not label a post-tool monitor a sandbox. Document exactly what is
and is not prevented (REQ-SAFE-004).
issues.acceptance_criteria: A written finding states which boundaries Pi/OMP can enforce, which it cannot, and what the fallback is; no mechanism is described as a sandbox unless it isolates at the OS or process level.

issues.title: establish one behavior execution path
issues.description:
Story 0.1. Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Remove or disable duplicate test-failure repair dispatch so one event cannot
start two competing fix agents (REQ-CQRS-002).

This is the highest-value item in Phase 0 and it is not speculative. Observed
live: the governed path rejected a direct write under `mode: propose` while the
continuation path repaired the same file in the same run. The duplicate path
also hid two P0 defects for three days by repairing code whenever the governed
path failed, so every session looked successful.

Scope:

- inventory the continuation queue, `BehaviorRunner`, `AutofixLoop`, matcher and
  event translator (input: the gap report)
- choose ONE governed route; remove or strictly isolate the other. Section 7 is
  explicit that silently merging them is not acceptable.
- produce the migration note mapping existing behavior fields to this contract

Do not keep both paths behind a flag that defaults to the ungoverned one.
issues.acceptance_criteria: One failure event demonstrably starts at most one workflow; a regression test proves it; the migration note exists.

issues.title: report where the tree differs from the CQRS spec
issues.description:
Section 8 requires this BEFORE implementation: inspect the checked-out branch
and report every difference between the specification and the actual tree.

Source: `docs/architecture/ensemble-behavior-cqrs-implementation-requirements.md`

Produce a written gap report covering at least:

- the continuation queue, `BehaviorRunner`, `AutofixLoop`, the matcher and the
  event translator: what each does today and which of them can mutate state
- every path that can write files or run shell/network operations
- which existing behavior.yaml fields map to the contract in section 3.1, and
  which have no equivalent (migration note)
- which of the 12 acceptance criteria in section 6 currently fail, with the
  evidence that shows it

Known starting points from live runs, all reproducible: two dispatch paths for
one event (br-dowt); propose mode leaving a fix applied (br-dowt); tool grants
not restricting tools (br-33co); verification trusting a defective runner
(br-gwww); per-invocation cwd confusion across call sites (br-nft8).

The report is the input to Story 0.1 and should be attached to this issue.
issues.acceptance_criteria: A written gap report exists naming every mutation path and every failing acceptance criterion with evidence; no implementation has begun.
